messages:
maria: Ran the long-context replay with yesterday's kernel-selector changes. Short summary: p95 regressed ~18% on prefill-heavy traces, median basically flat. posting the quick perf snapshot and logs below.
jon: Ugh. Is this across all models or specific to longseq workloads? :thinking:
maria: It's reproducible on the longmix replay (prefill_ratio >= 0.6). Not seen on short-context synthetic. Only showed up when we enable the new kernel scoring path.
maria: Perf snippet (two runs, before -> after):
```
cmd: ./replay_harness --trace=longmix --seed=7 --kernelselect=baseline
p50: 120ms
p95: 420ms
p99: 860ms
---
cmd: ./replay_harness --trace=longmix --seed=7 --kernelselect=adaptive
p50: 118ms
p95: 496ms
p99: 890ms
notes: regression concentrated in first 10 tokens after prefill (prefill-dominant)
```
kai: Can you paste the kernel-chooser debug log around a regression sample? want to see chosen kernels and batch sizes.
maria: paste of chooser snippet (trimmed):
```
[12:03:21] chose kernel: conv_kv_quant_fp16 (score=0.82)
[12:03:21] batch_estimate: tokens=1536, batch_count=6
[12:03:21] predicted_mem: 4.1GB, fallback: none
[12:03:21] execute kernel conv_kv_quant_fp16 -> 7.2ms per step
```
sam: hypothesis: the adaptive selector is preferring a quant FP16 kernel that does great on short decoding, but its KV handling (memcopy / cache layout) is worse for prefill-dominant sequences. KV memcpy + eviction thrash could show up as p95 tail.
kai: +1. I looked at the perf flamegraph for the run — hot path is in `kv_cache::apply_prefill` memcpy and then `kernel_wrapper::prepare_kv` sync. blame points to `memmove` for large KV slices.
maria: flamegraph link: https://perf.internal/runs/2123456789/flame (raw snapshot attached to the run). dev-bot also recorded the build id: 2026.3-kernelselect-b
dev-bot: build 2026.3-kernelselect-b deployed to test-cluster-4 at 2026-03-15T12:00:03Z :robot_face:
ops: to make this apples-to-apples, can you force the old kernel on the same trace? `--force-kernel=baseline_kernel` and compare. we need a deterministic repro for an issue.
maria: did exactly that. forced baseline vs forced adaptive on same trace, same seed. results below (single-run numbers):
```
forced=baseline_kernel p95: 422ms
forced=adaptive_kernel  p95: 497ms
delta: +17.8%
```
jon: nice. can you also run with `--kv-warmup=off` and `--kv-chunk=64k` to see if chunking/warmup params change it? that'll tell if it's mem-copy granularity.
maria: running a quick sweep now, will post numbers in ~10m. :coffee:
(maria later): quick sweep:
```
--kv-warmup=on --kv-chunk=256k p95: 494ms
--kv-warmup=off --kv-chunk=64k  p95: 428ms
```
notes: turning warmup off reduces the regression significantly; suggests warmup path causes extra copies for large prefill.
sam: OK that's very suggestive. warmup path probably triggers an extra temporary buffer for those kernels. maybe the adaptive kernel assumed streaming prefill and set up a different io path.
kai: action items: 1) add microbench that reproduces kv memcpy cost for prefill sizes (256k, 512k) 2) add a counter in runtime to count extra temp allocations in warmup path 3) run with 1% sample through replay harness to get wall-clock per-step distribution.
ops: created a short job template for replay-harness with `--sample-rate=0.01 --trace=longmix --force-kernel=adaptive` (job id job/infra-8724). use that for stress runs.
maria: created GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/4521 — added logs, perf diff, and warmup vs off numbers. assigned to @kai and @sam. :thumbsup:
jon: label it perf/regression and add the regression experiment commands so QE can rerun. Also cc infra on the job so we can schedule larger runs.
kai: I'll pick it up. plan: repro microbench + add instrumentation (temp allocs) -> if confirmed, patch kernel wrapper to avoid extra memcpy for warmup path. estimate 1-2 days.
maria: cool. thanks everyone. if anyone sees other odd long-context tails from the same build please add comments to #4521 and paste the raw run id.
ops: noted. will keep the test cluster pinned to baseline for canary a/b until fix lands. :lock:
jon: thanks — good triage. closing the loop in the issue when we have a candidate fix.
